name: Noxfield ChemShell Overcoat
description: On the Shelf, particularly near the old industrial zones where remediation has been ongoing since 2140 and is nowhere near finished, a coat that offers some protection against particulate and chemical exposure is not a luxury — it is basic survival equipment. The Noxfield ChemShell is a full-length overcoat made from a laminated polyfilm material that resists low-grade chemical splash, acid rain, and industrial particulate. It is not a true hazmat suit; it will not protect you from serious exposure. But for daily life near the toxic buffer zones, it provides meaningful mitigation. The coat is stiff, crinkles when you move, and comes in a yellow-gray color that fades to a dingy beige within a season of use. The neck seals with a hook-and-bar closure that pulls tight against vapor. Shelf residents resell and repair these constantly — patches of different ChemShell generations make some coats look like textile archaeology.
functionality: Low-grade chemical splash resistance. Particulate barrier rated for PM2.5 and above. Not rated for sustained chemical exposure.
what_it_says: You live near something that can hurt you and you do not have the option to move away from it. This coat is evidence of a structural failure that predates your birth.
manufacturer: Noxfield Safety (Tier 1 distributed brand, manufacturer unclear)
story_hooks: Noxfield's actual manufacturing source is deliberately obscured — some units are knockoffs of knockoffs, and a recent batch has been circulating that fails its rated chemical resistance at concentrations well below spec

A Shelf community organizer has been collecting worn ChemShell coats as physical evidence of long-term toxic exposure — the coat's polyfilm absorbs and retains trace chemical signatures that standard medical testing misses

Someone has been leaving fully functional ChemShell overcoats in good condition at specific Shelf distribution points with no identifying information — Shelf residents call the anonymous donor the Coat Ghost
related_entities: Arcturus Defense Solutions ChemoShield BX-2 Dermal Toxin Barrier Implant

physical_description.visual_profile: A long, utilitarian overcoat with a distinctly industrial silhouette. The laminated polyfilm creates a stiff, almost architectural drape that hangs away from the body. Visually reads as protective gear rather than fashion — imposing, angular, deliberately unglamorous. The material has a slight sheen that catches light unevenly.
physical_description.fit: Loose and intentionally oversized to allow layering underneath and unrestricted movement. Sleeve length extends to the wrist; coat reaches mid-calf. Cut is straight and boxy with no waist definition. Built for function over form.
physical_description.primary_material: Laminated polyfilm composite — a synthetic membrane bonded to reinforced textile backing. Acoustically crunches and crinkles with movement. Feels plasticky and slightly stiff to the touch.
physical_description.texture: Smooth outer laminate with subtle micro-texture from the weave beneath. Develops a dull, worn sheen with age. Creases hold permanently. Patches of different ages create visible quilted or slightly raised sections.
physical_description.color_scheme: Factory yellow-gray transitioning to dingy beige and gray after weathering. Some specimens show darker chemical staining around the hem and sleeve cuffs. Patches in mismatched tones of gray, tan, and faded yellow from repair grafts.
physical_description.closures: Central full-length zipper (often replaced or reinforced on older coats). Neck seals with hook-and-bar Velcro-style closure that tightens around the throat. Wrist cuffs have friction-fit elastic or snap closures.
distinctive_features: Oversized hood with reinforced brim and sealed seams
Multiple external pockets with sealed zippers
Visible patching and repair work — textile archaeology of different ChemShell generations
Noxfield branded tab on inner collar (often worn or removed)
Faded or worn Noxfield Safety logo on left chest
Chemical staining or discoloration on lower sections typical of heavy use
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional. Affordable protective equipment for working-class residents in remediation zones. Resale and repair economy suggests Tier 5 sub-grade wearing generations-old patched versions.
physical_description.cultural_context: Marks the wearer as a Shelf resident, industrial zone worker, or remediation technician. Signals practical survival in contaminated areas rather than status. Worn by those for whom chemical exposure is daily reality, not exception. Heavy resale culture — seeing one suggests economic constraints and resourcefulness.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn and weathered. Most in circulation show visible patching, faded coloring, and accumulated chemical staining. Zippers are often replaced or reinforced. Creasing is permanent. A pristine ChemShell is rare; broken-in is the baseline.

image_prompt: A weathered yellow-gray laminated polyfilm overcoat on a lean model standing in a derelict industrial setting, toxic buffer zone aesthetic. Moody sodium-vapor lighting casting sickly amber-green tones. Visible patches of different textile repairs cover the sleeves and torso. The coat crinkles audibly in the still air. Dark cinderblock wall with chemical staining and remediation markers visible behind. Gritty, utilitarian, worn — beauty in survival gear.
